If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3–5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment shifts from negative to positive over 3–5 days, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment remains flat (0.33–0.67) across recent days, apply no adjustment to forecast in early horizon (1–7 days) but slightly dampen upward bias in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in last 2–3 days, increase forecast by 1–2% in late horizon (21–30 days) to reflect strong conviction, but cap at 3% to avoid overfitting.

If sentiment drops to 0.00 in last 2–3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% in late horizon (21–30 days) to reflect bearish sentiment, but avoid below 60% of prior peak to prevent extreme underestimation.
